originalGoal: Assess whether this service is ready for release without changing application source. Audit server/auth.ts for authentication/session expiry vulnerabilities and write reports/auth.md with evidence, reproduction cases, severity and recommended fixes. Separately audit server/storage.ts for crash consistency and data-loss risks and write reports/storage.md with failure scenarios, severity and recommended fixes. Produce reports/release.md using both reports to prioritize blockers, explain tradeoffs and recommend a release decision. Do not implement the fixes in this assessment.

nodes.name: auth_session_audit
nodes.task:
Read-only security audit of authentication and session handling in this service, focused on `server/auth.ts` (session store, `authenticate`, and how `server/users.ts` / `server/config.ts` interact with it). Deliver `reports/auth.md`.

Scope: authentication correctness and session-expiry vulnerabilities — e.g. whether `expiresAt` is ever enforced on lookup, session creation/revocation and unbounded growth, token generation/entropy and guessability, empty or reused session state across requests/processes, and error behavior for unknown or expired tokens. Follow the session/auth semantics that exist in the repo; note where `server/config.ts` supplies timing or lifetime values rather than assuming them.

Constraints: do not modify any application source, config, or tests — the only file you create is `reports/auth.md`. Any reproduction must be non-destructive and must not require editing tracked files; if you run code to confirm behavior, record the exact commands and their real output in the report.

`reports/auth.md` must contain, per finding: title, affected file/lines, evidence (quoted code plus command/output where available), a concrete reproduction case, severity with rationale (impact + likelihood), exploitability assumptions, and a recommended fix described as a design change (do not implement it). Separate confirmed findings from suspicions that need product input. End with the top authentication blockers for a release decision.

nodes.name: storage_crash_consistency_audit
nodes.task:
Read-only durability audit of persistence in this service, focused on `server/storage.ts` (its use of `node:fs` write paths) and its callers such as `server/users.ts` and `src/importer.ts` if they persist data. Deliver `reports/storage.md`.

Scope: crash consistency and data-loss risk — e.g. atomicity of writes (partial/truncated files after process or machine crash), absence of temp-file + rename or `fsync` on file and parent directory, destructive overwrite of existing data without backup, error swallowing, concurrent-write interleaving, and behavior when the target path/directory is missing or unwritable. Base severity on what the repository actually does; do not invent guarantees the code does not claim.

Constraints: do not modify any application source, config, or tests, and do not write scratch data into tracked locations — the only file you create is `reports/storage.md`. Verify claims with non-destructive probes or reasoning about the code path, recording exact commands and real output where used.

`reports/storage.md` must contain, per finding: title, affected file/lines, evidence, a concrete failure scenario (what the process/host does at which instant, and the resulting on-disk state), severity with rationale, the blast radius in terms of data loss or corruption, and a recommended fix described as a design change (do not implement it). Separate confirmed findings from items needing further instrumentation, and end with the top storage blockers for a release decision.

nodes.name: release_decision
nodes.task:
Produce the release-readiness assessment for this service by synthesizing the two audit reports. Consumes `reports/auth.md` (authentication/session-expiry findings) and `reports/storage.md` (crash-consistency/data-loss findings); deliver `reports/release.md`.

Do not modify application source, config, or tests, and do not perform new experiments or re-derive the audits — work from the evidence the two reports already record. If a finding lacks evidence in its report, do not silently upgrade or invent support for it: cite the gap and request revision from the report owner.

`reports/release.md` should contain:
1. A one-line release recommendation (ship / ship behind mitigation / block) with the deciding rationale.
2. A prioritized blocker table across both domains: finding, source from `server/auth.ts` or `server/storage.ts`, severity as reported, exploit or failure likelihood, user-visible blast radius, and why it is or is not release-blocking. Where the two reports rate severities inconsistently for comparable risk, reconcile explicitly and say which you adopted.
3. Tradeoffs: cost/risk of shipping now with documented workarounds versus delaying, and which mitigations are operational (config, process supervision, deployment practice) versus code changes — noting that code changes are out of scope for this assessment.
4. Recommended fix sequencing with owner areas, marked as recommendations only, since no fixes are implemented here.
5. Open questions / unproven inferences carried over from both reports.

Also confirm the assessment stayed read-only: check that `server/auth.ts` and `server/storage.ts` still contain the code quoted as evidence in the reports (i.e. no fix has already been applied that would invalidate the findings) and note the result. Keep the report concise and link to the detailed files rather than restating them. End with the release decision on the final line.
